record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: In high-dimensional data, can one design worst-case algorithms for computing the Gabriel graph or the rectangular-influence graph of a training set {X, Y} in o(dn^3) time?

evidence.quote: Finding algorithms for computing these graphs in o(dn3) worst-case time is an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S = \{x_1, \ldots, x_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite set of $n$ points in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space (think of $d$ as large, possibly comparable to $n$). Define the following two proximity graphs on the vertex set $S$:

1. The Gabriel graph $G(S)$: an unordered pair $\{x_i, x_j\}$ is an edge if and only if the closed Euclidean ball whose diameter is the segment $\overline{x_i x_j}$ (i.e. the ball of radius $\|x_i - x_j\|/2$ centered at the midpoint $(x_i+x_j)/2$) contains no other point of $S$ in its interior. Equivalently, $\{x_i, x_j\}$ is an edge iff for every $x_k \in S \setminus \{x_i, x_j\}$,
$$\|x_i - x_j\|^2 \le \|x_i - x_k\|^2 + \|x_j - x_k\|^2.$$

2. The rectangular-influence graph $R(S)$: an unordered pair $\{x_i, x_j\}$ is an edge if and only if the open axis-aligned hyperrectangle (in the coordinate system in which $x_i$ and $x_j$ are taken as a pair of opposite corners) determined by $x_i$ and $x_j$ contains no other point of $S$. Equivalently, $\{x_i, x_j\}$ is an edge iff there is no $x_k \in S\setminus\{x_i,x_j\}$ with each coordinate of $x_k$ strictly between the corresponding coordinates of $x_i$ and $x_j$.

A straightforward brute-force algorithm computes either graph in $O(d\,n^3)$ worst-case time by checking, for each of the $\binom{n}{2}$ candidate edges, the defining condition against all remaining $n-2$ points (each check costing $O(d)$ time).

Question: Does there exist a deterministic algorithm that, given any input $S \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of $n$ points, computes the Gabriel graph $G(S)$ in worst-case time $o(d\,n^3)$? Likewise, does there exist such an algorithm computing the rectangular-influence graph $R(S)$ in worst-case time $o(d\,n^3)$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned standard results on planar Gabriel graph construction (e.g. $O(n\log n)$ via Delaunay triangulation in 2D) and brute-force $O(n^3)$ approaches, but no algorithm or hardness result was located that beats $O(d\,n^3)$ worst-case time for either the Gabriel graph or the rectangular-influence graph in arbitrary high dimension. The question therefore appears to remain unresolved in the literature accessible via search.

status_evidence.title: Gabriel graph - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Gabriel graphs naturally generalize to higher dimensions, with the empty disks replaced by empty closed balls. The fast (sub-cubic) construction via Delaunay triangulation is given for the planar Euclidean case.
status_evidence.claim: Efficient construction is established in 2D; high-dimensional case is not addressed by a known sub-$O(dn^3)$ algorithm.

status_evidence.title: Optimizing the Gabriel graph construction algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of Gabriel graph construction algorithms, with cubic worst-case time for general/high-dimensional inputs.
status_evidence.claim: No high-dimensional algorithm beating $O(dn^3)$ worst-case is reported.

status_evidence.title: High-dimensional labeled data analysis with Gabriel graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Uses Gabriel graphs for high-dimensional learning; relies on the brute-force $O(dn^3)$-style construction.
